title: China’s Strategic Reassessment of India
gist: Stimson Center's Yun Sun reports, from 10 research trips and exchanges with Chinese experts, that Beijing is reassessing India as a middle power with unmalleable strategy after the US turn away from India, and is leaning on trade dependence ($151.1 billion bilateral trade, $112.1 billion Indian deficit) rather than empowerment. She sees the current thaw as limited and potentially short-lived, hinging on Indian domestic politics and future US policy.

themes.theme: China's view of India's power status

insights.claim: With the US less inclined to elevate India, Chinese strategists are returning to the view that India is a middle power with great potential that its strategic culture will keep it from realizing.
insights.speaker: Yun Sun
insights.so_what: Chinese policy toward India will be less deferential if Beijing sees India as a weaker, less aligned player.

insights.claim: India's GDP is only about 20 percent of China's, but Beijing learned from its own 1970s-2000s experience that US support can rapidly elevate a country, which is why US backing of India in the first Trump and Biden administrations alarmed China.
insights.speaker: Yun Sun
insights.so_what: US policy shifts toward India are a lead indicator for Chinese threat perception and for India's growth narrative.

insights.claim: China believes it followed a policy of accommodation toward India, citing Xi-Modi outreach in 2018, 2024 and 2025 and 280,000 visas issued to Indians in 2025 versus 2,000 issued by India to Chinese nationals.
insights.speaker: Yun Sun
insights.so_what: Beijing frames its restraint as proof it is unwilling to sour ties, relevant to how it will justify future retaliation.

insights.claim: Chinese specialists judge India's strategic choices unmalleable: India refused to abandon Russian energy and economic ties and is reluctant to confront China in a Taiwan contingency, which cuts India's value as a US partner and reduces China's anxiety about an India-US alliance.
insights.speaker: Yun Sun
insights.so_what: Lowers the odds of an India-US military alignment against China, limiting deterrent value of that relationship.

insights.claim: Chinese experts widely invoke the Indian concept of Dana (almsgiving) to explain India's perceived ungratefulness, reading acceptance of US aid as India doing the giver a favor.
insights.speaker: Yun Sun
insights.so_what: Cultural framing shapes Chinese expectations of Indian reciprocity; the author notes the argument is debatable.

insights.claim: India's foreign policy community distinguishes 'like-minded' from 'same-minded' countries and favors issue-based alignments over permanent alliances.
insights.speaker: Yun Sun
insights.so_what: Expect India to keep multi-aligning with Europe, Japan, Canada and other middle powers rather than choose a bloc.

insights.claim: In fiscal year 2025-26 China-India trade reached $151.1 billion with a $112.1 billion Indian deficit, meaning 87 percent of trade is Chinese exports to India.
insights.speaker: Yun Sun
insights.so_what: Large structural deficit is both a sore spot for India and Chinese leverage.

insights.claim: India imports Chinese materials, parts and equipment to make finished goods for export to developed markets, so its deficit with China translates into surpluses with partners like the US and decoupling would inflict significant pain on Indian industry.
insights.speaker: Yun Sun
insights.so_what: India's export manufacturing remains exposed to Chinese inputs; supply shocks could repeat the US 2025 tariff-war experience.

insights.claim: Unlike elsewhere in South Asia (agricultural technology in Nepal, green tech and digital economy in Pakistan, Smart Bangladesh), China's economic engagement with India lacks 'empowerment', suggesting a deliberate avoidance of lifting India's technological productivity.
insights.speaker: Yun Sun
insights.so_what: Chinese capital and technology transfer into India is unlikely; Indian investment restrictions on Chinese firms look durable.

insights.claim: Sino-Indian relations have a ceiling because of Pakistan, border disputes and regional competition, but possibly no floor given the history of conflict; the current rewarming may expire sooner than expected because both sides keep options open pending US policy.
insights.speaker: Yun Sun
insights.so_what: Treat the thaw as tactical; border or Pakistan-related flare-ups remain a tail risk.
insights.locator: Where Do China and India Go from Here?

insights.claim: Chinese observers see rising tension between Modi and the RSS, and any successor is unlikely to match Modi's popularity, making Indian internal cohesion a key uncertainty.
insights.speaker: Yun Sun
insights.so_what: Indian succession politics is a hidden variable for India's foreign policy consistency.
insights.locator: Where Do China and India Go from Here?

insights.claim: If Chinese anxiety about the US-India relationship has diminished, the deterrent value Washington derived from it has fallen too, a cost of current policy that nobody is counting.
insights.speaker: Yun Sun
insights.so_what: Signals a hidden cost to the US shift away from India.
insights.quote: a cost of the current policy that nobody is counting

insights.claim: Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau warned in March 2026 at the Raisina Dialogue that the US would not repeat its 'China mistake' with India.
insights.speaker: Yun Sun
insights.so_what: Indicates US officials still see India as a hedge against Chinese strength.
